PATIENT INFORMATION

Notice of Privacy Practices

Prepared October 4, 2026 · Effective date: pending practice adoption

Practice review required. Confirm the legal entity, designated privacy contact, effective date, actual uses of records, and applicable California protections before adopting this draft. It does not replace an existing notice.

THIS NOTICE DESCRIBES HOW MEDICAL INFORMATION ABOUT YOU MAY BE USED AND DISCLOSED AND HOW YOU CAN GET ACCESS TO THIS INFORMATION. PLEASE REVIEW IT CAREFULLY.

Who this notice covers

This proposed notice covers dental care provided by Tooth Cube Dental at the address below. The legal entity operating the practice must be confirmed before adoption.

How information is used

  • Treatment: We may share relevant records with another clinician caring for you, such as sending dental images to a treating specialist.
  • Payment: We may send treatment and billing information to your insurer to process a claim.
  • Practice operations: We may review records to assess care quality or use information to manage appointments. Service providers handling protected information on our behalf must meet applicable privacy requirements.

Other permitted or required disclosures

Subject to legal conditions, information may be disclosed for public health reporting; reporting abuse, neglect, or domestic violence; health oversight and licensing; approved research; responding to court proceedings or lawful law-enforcement requests; workers’ compensation; organ donation; coroners and funeral directors; preventing a serious threat to health or safety; and authorized military, national-security, or correctional activities. We also disclose information when required by law, including to HHS for compliance investigations. A request alone does not automatically authorize disclosure.

More protective federal or California rules may restrict these uses, including rules covering certain sensitive records and minors’ confidential care. Information released to a recipient may be redisclosed and may no longer be protected by HIPAA, although other laws may still apply.

Your choices and written permission

Where permitted, we may share relevant information with people involved in your care or payment when you agree or have an opportunity to object. If you cannot express a preference, limited sharing may occur based on professional judgment and your best interests.

Most uses of psychotherapy notes, marketing uses, and disclosures involving the sale of protected health information require written authorization, subject to legal exceptions. Other uses not described here also require authorization. You may revoke an authorization in writing, except to the extent action has already been taken in reliance on it.

If records protected by 42 CFR Part 2 are received, they cannot be used in proceedings against you without the required written consent or a qualifying court order and accompanying legal process. Any permitted fundraising use of those records requires an advance opportunity to opt out.

Your privacy rights

Contact the office to exercise these rights. We may verify your identity and request a written application where permitted.

  • Inspect or obtain records: Request your dental and billing records in an available format. Applicable deadlines, limited exceptions, and permitted copying fees apply. If access is denied, we will explain the reason and any available review rights. California law may give you faster access than HIPAA.
  • Request corrections: Ask us to amend information you believe is incorrect or incomplete. We will explain a denial in writing and how to submit a statement of disagreement.
  • Request confidential contact: Ask us to communicate at a different address or by a particular method. We will accommodate reasonable requests.
  • Request limits: Ask us to limit certain uses or disclosures. We are not required to agree to every request. When you pay an item or service in full out of pocket and request it, we must restrict disclosure to your health plan for payment or operations unless disclosure is required by law.
  • Receive an accounting: Ask for a list of certain disclosures during the preceding six years. Exceptions include many treatment, payment, operations, and authorized disclosures. One accounting in a 12-month period is free; we will tell you about any permitted charge for additional requests.
  • Obtain this notice: Ask for a paper copy even if you previously agreed to electronic delivery.
  • Use a representative: A person legally authorized to act for you may exercise your rights, subject to applicable limits.

Our responsibilities

We must protect your health information, provide notice of our duties and privacy practices, follow the notice currently in effect, and notify you when a breach of unsecured protected health information requires notification.

We may change this notice and apply changes to information we already hold, where permitted by law. A revised notice will show its effective date and be available on this website and from our office.

Questions or complaints

Ask our office for the designated privacy contact. Practice to confirm the responsible name or title before adoption.

You may also file a privacy complaint with HHS, call 1-877-696-6775, or write to HHS Office for Civil Rights, 200 Independence Avenue SW, Washington, DC 20201. We will not retaliate for a complaint.

Draft references: HHS model notice and HIPAA Privacy Rule. Review California-specific protections and current court rulings before adoption.
